gap: No result ChatGPT got states a tested figure for any 1,000 Wh station under $400: named reviewers got 856 Wh from the Pecron E1000LFP (The Solar Lab, by arithmetic), 880 Wh from the DJI Power 1000 V2 (OutdoorGearLab) and 903 Wh from the Bluetti Elite 100 mini (The Cool Down), and The Solar Lab measured the Pecron and DJI burning about 18 W with AC on and nothing plugged in against 13.5 W for the Bluetti.
standout_why: I opened eight of the result pages: PopSci's Black Friday roundup (the one ChatGPT cited), GearJunkie, OutletPicks, Backup Power Hub, Solar Generator Prices, JuiceBench and WattLab Review. None gives a measured usable Wh, efficiency, idle draw or timed charge for any candidate; they carry rated capacity and prices only. Backup Power Hub and WattLab use a generic 'capacity × 0.85' formula, and ChatGPT's own answer calls its 800–900 Wh 'a planning estimate, not a tested result'. GearJunkie has test notes only for the Anker C1000 and Jackery 1000 Plus, both over $400. Not opened: TechRadar, The Drive, SFGate, Station Arena, powerstations.reviews, batteryplaces, wattpowerstation, dealnews.
decides: Usable energy does not split the three: 856–903 Wh is a spread of about 5%, measured at different loads by different reviewers, so the pick still turns on AC watts and price. That supports the desk placement of DJI (2,600 W) first and the 700 W Bluetti as the light-load pick; The Cool Down saw the Bluetti shut down at 900 W. Idle draw adds one thing: The Solar Lab's 18 W figure cost the Pecron about 430 Wh in 24 hours with AC on and no load, so for a router or CPAP left on all day the Bluetti's 13.5 W is the better fit. No named measurement of our ALLPOWERS P1800 turned up, so its row can carry maker figures only.

findings.label: Efficiency under high load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Pecron E1000LFP Power Station Review: Solid Performance for Just $379?
findings.note: The Solar Lab ran a 1,556 W load: expected 39 min, 'it actually ran for 33 minutes, making it 84% efficient'. The 856 Wh is my arithmetic (1,556 W × 33/60 h); the review gives no Wh figure. Page shows no author or date, only © 2026, and carries an affiliate code.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC on, no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Pecron E1000LFP Power Station Review: Solid Performance for Just $379?
findings.note: Battery fell from 87% to 45% in 24 h with the AC inverter on and nothing plugged in. With only DC on it fell from 45% to 23%, about 9.5 W. Review undated.

findings.label: AC charge to full and overload (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 'almost exactly one hour' to full; held 2,200 W for about 5 s before shutting down
findings.source_title: Pecron E1000LFP Power Station Review: Solid Performance for Just $379?
findings.note: Pecron advertises 1.3 h per the review. Inverter is rated 1,800 W with a 3,000 W advertised surge. No dB figure ('a medium level of noise'); no UPS time. Review undated.

findings.label: Measured energy output (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, published 2026-07-23. The test load is not stated on the page. The same table lists Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 890 Wh, EcoFlow Delta 3 870 Wh and Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 910 Wh, all over $400 today per the desk notes.

findings.label: Measured charge time and weight (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: The text says 59 minutes; the spec table says 0.9 hr and 1,041 Wh/hr charging speed. The text also calls the inverter '2,200 watts' while the table says 2,600 W: an inconsistency on the page. No dB figure.

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 portable power station review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 'The unit delivered 82% efficiency'; 'Idle consumption came in at around 18 watts'. Test load not stated. It also reports wall charging at 'around 1,500 watts'. No author or date shown.

findings.label: Low-load discharge and charge (DroneXL)
findings.value: about 80% efficiency at 195 W ('just over four hours', two runs); 80% charge in 37 min at 1,400–1,450 W
findings.note: Russ (51 Drones), published 2026-01-08. 100% to 0% twice at about 195 W. 195 W × 4 h = 780 Wh as a floor; no Wh figure is given.

findings.label: Usable capacity (The Cool Down)
findings.value: 903 Wh of the advertised 1,004 Wh, 'roughly 90% efficiency'
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 100 mini backup battery review (The Cool Down)
findings.note: Vivian Tran, published 2026-09-06. Test load not stated. In separate load checks the unit shut down at 900 W (rated 700 W); wall charging reached about 700 W.

findings.label: Idle draw, charge time, overload (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 13.5 W idle; about 2 hours empty to full at up to 700 W; 'over 1,000W for a decent amount of time'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini Review: Small, Simple, and Effective?
findings.note: The review also says '97% efficient' with no load or method given; that conflicts with The Cool Down's 90%, so I would not print the 97% without that caveat. No author or date shown; carries an affiliate code.

findings.label: Efficiency under high load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: OUPES Mega 1 Review: Affordable and Powerful or Too Good to Be True?
findings.note: Sustained 1,779 W load: 'actual runtime was 27 minutes, equating to a 79% efficiency rating' against about 34 min expected. The 800 Wh is my arithmetic (1,779 W × 27/60 h). Fans described as 'very, very loud', no dB. Review undated; today's price not read, so its place under $400 is unverified.

findings.label: Idle draw as a share of the battery over a day
findings.source_title: Pecron E1000LFP Power Station Review: Solid Performance for Just $379?
findings.note: My arithmetic from The Solar Lab's idle figures (18 W Pecron and DJI, 13.5 W Elite 100 mini; the mini's is at https://www.thesolarlab.com/review/bluetti-elite-100-mini). The Pecron's 24-hour drop of about 430 Wh was observed directly.

findings.label: Method caveat for a side-by-side table
findings.value: Loads differ: 1,556 W (Pecron), 1,779 W (OUPES), 195 W (DJI, DroneXL), unstated (OutdoorGearLab, The Cool Down)
findings.note: The figures come from four reviewers with different methods, so each should be shown with its reviewer and load, not ranked as like-for-like.
